transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

I'm here because I spend so much time checking and rechecking how I look at the gym and before going out that it’s taking over my days. It’s gotten to the point where it’s just exhausting, and I feel like I can't control it anymore.

When you check your appearance, is it mainly because you fear something is wrong with your body or face, or is it more a repeated urge you feel you have to do even when you know it may not be necessary?

It's because I genuinely feel like something is wrong with my face. When I look in the mirror, all I can focus on is how crooked my face looks and how weird my jawline is from the side. I feel this constant need to keep checking so I can try to hide that messed-up side before anyone else sees me.
Do you spend a lot of time worrying about a specific flaw in your appearance that others may not notice, and does this worry make you avoid social situations or looking in mirrors?

Yes, I worry constantly about my face looking crooked and my jawline being weird, which my friends claim they don't even notice. I don't avoid mirrors—in fact, I spend hours obsessively checking them to try and fix how I look—but I definitely avoid social situations like soccer matches and salsa nights when I'm worried about being seen from the wrong angle.

Do you also have unwanted intrusive thoughts or fears about other things, like contamination, harm, or needing things to be perfectly ordered, that lead you to do rituals such as checking, washing, or repeating actions?
No, I don't have any fears or rituals about things like contamination or order. All of my worries and the checking I do are strictly focused on my appearance and how my face looks.
Do you feel that the concern about your face or jawline is excessive or possibly not as noticeable to others, or are you completely convinced that it is truly deformed?

Even though my friends say they don't see anything wrong, I am completely convinced that my face is crooked and my jawline looks messed up. To me, it feels completely real and highly noticeable, which is why I feel this overwhelming need to hide it and avoid being seen.
Have you ever had any other unusual beliefs, like feeling that people are talking about you, watching you, or trying to harm you, even when there is no clear evidence?

No, I don't experience those kinds of feelings, like people trying to harm me or watching me in a creepy way. However, I do constantly worry that people are looking at me and judging my face or jawline when I'm out in public.
When you worry that people are judging your face, do you ever believe they are specifically talking about you, spying on you, or trying to harm you, or is it only about how your appearance looks?

No, it is entirely about how my appearance looks, and I don't believe anyone is spying on me or trying to harm me. My anxiety is purely focused on people seeing my crooked face and weird jawline from the wrong angle and thinking I look wrong.
Do you recognize that your concern about your face may be exaggerated or not as noticeable to others, or are you completely certain that it is truly deformed?

My sister and friends keep telling me they don't see anything wrong, but to me, it feels completely real, glaringly obvious, and deformed. It is really hard to believe them because when I look in the mirror or at photos, the crookedness of my face and jawline looks undeniably wrong.

Have you ever been able to consider that your face or jawline might actually look normal and that this fear could be exaggerated, even a little? Or are you completely certain it is truly deformed despite what others say?

Even though my friends keep telling me they don't see anything wrong, it feels completely real and undeniable to me. When I look at photos or in the mirror, I am absolutely convinced my face is crooked and my jawline is weird. Because of that, it's almost impossible for me to believe that it might actually look normal.

Have you ever had any other fixed beliefs that other people say are clearly untrue, such as believing someone is targeting you or that something outside your appearance is wrong with you? Or is the only issue your face and jawline looking deformed to you?

No, I don't have any other beliefs like that, and I definitely don't feel like anyone is targeting me. The only issue is my face and jawline looking crooked and deformed from certain angles. All of my distress is completely focused on how my appearance looks.
Have you ever been able to think that your face or jawline might actually look normal, even for a moment, or are you completely certain it is truly deformed no matter what others say?

I've never been able to think it looks normal, not even for a second. Even though my friends say they don't see anything wrong, when I look in the mirror or at photos, I am completely convinced that my face is crooked and my jawline looks weird. I just can't see it any other way because it feels completely real to me.
Have you ever suspected that your concern about your face might be a false belief or an exaggeration, even briefly, or are you completely certain it is truly deformed despite what others tell you?

I'm not really sure how to answer that, because I've never really thought about it that way. To me, it just feels so completely real when I look in the mirror, so I've never really questioned whether it's an exaggeration or not.

When you feel certain your face is crooked, have you ever been able to consider that this might be an overreaction or not actually true, even a little, or do you believe it with complete certainty despite what others tell you?
Honestly, I'm not sure how to answer that because it's just so hard to think any other way. When I look at myself, it feels completely real, so I can't really imagine it not being true.

When you think about your face being crooked, do you ever consider that this might be an overreaction or that other people may be right that it looks normal, even a little? Or are you completely certain it is truly deformed?

My friends and family keep telling me it looks normal, but I am completely convinced it is deformed and crooked. When I look in the mirror or at photos, it feels so entirely real to me that I just can't believe their reassurances. To me, the flaws are undeniably there.
Have you ever thought that this might be a false belief or that your face could actually be normal, even for a moment, or are you completely certain it is deformed despite what others tell you?

My friends and family constantly tell me they don't see anything wrong, but to me, the defect feels completely real. When I look in the mirror or at photos, I am entirely convinced that my face is crooked and my jawline is weird. It's just almost impossible for me to believe otherwise when I can see it so clearly right there.
Have you ever heard voices, felt controlled by outside forces, or believed that other people were deliberately trying to harm or spy on you because of your face?
No, I've never heard voices, felt controlled by outside forces, or believed anyone was spying on or trying to harm me. My worries are strictly about how my face and jawline look, and nothing else.
Have you ever thought there was a chance your face might actually look normal, even a small chance, or are you completely certain it is truly deformed?

Even though my friends constantly tell me they don't see anything wrong, the crookedness and weird jawline seem completely real and undeniable when I look at myself. It is incredibly hard to believe it might be normal because of how obvious the flaws look to me, especially when I zoom in on photos.
Do you think there is any chance at all that your face and jawline might actually look normal, or are you completely certain they are truly deformed despite what others say?

Even though my friends say they don't see anything wrong, to me, the flaws feel completely real and undeniable. I will sit there for hours zooming in on photos and picking apart my jawline and crooked face, which makes it impossible for me to believe it actually looks normal.
Have you ever been able to consider, even briefly, that your face might actually look normal and that this concern could be exaggerated, or are you completely certain it is truly deformed?

While my friends tell me they don't see anything wrong, it feels completely real and undeniable to me. When I look in the mirror or at pictures, I am absolutely convinced my face is crooked and my jawline is weird. It is just almost impossible for me to believe otherwise when I see it so clearly.
Do you think there is any real chance that your face might actually look normal, or are you completely certain it is deformed despite what other people tell you?

Even though my friends and family tell me nothing is wrong, I am completely convinced my face is crooked and my jawline is deformed. I just can't ignore what I clearly see with my own eyes in photos and mirrors.
Have you ever had even a brief moment of doubt that your face might actually look normal, or are you completely certain it is truly deformed despite what others tell you?

I'm not really sure how to answer that, because I've never really thought about it in those terms. It just feels so completely real to me when I look in the mirror that the doubt never really crosses my mind.
Have you ever been able to consider that your face might actually look normal, even for a moment, or are you completely certain it is truly deformed despite what others tell you?

Even though my friends and family tell me they don't see anything wrong, I find it almost impossible to believe them. When I look at myself, the crookedness of my face and my weird jawline feel completely real and obvious to me, making it feel like a genuine deformity that I just can't ignore.
Do you believe other people can clearly see the flaw in your face too, or do you think they just don’t notice it even though it is definitely there?

Even though my friends say they don't see anything wrong, I am convinced the crookedness and weird jawline are definitely there and very noticeable. I feel like if people see me from the wrong angle, it will be completely obvious to them. That is why I go to such lengths to hide my face or just avoid being seen entirely.
When you think about the flaw in your face, do you believe it could be your mind overestimating it, or are you completely certain it is truly deformed and real?

While my friends tell me they don't see anything wrong, to me it feels completely real, glaringly obvious, and deformed. When I look in the mirror or at photos, I see a highly visible, 'messed-up' crookedness and jawline that I feel I absolutely must hide.
Have you ever had other fixed beliefs that people are watching you, talking about you, or trying to harm you, or is the concern only about your appearance?

No, my concern is strictly about my appearance, and I don't believe anyone is trying to harm me or talking about me for other reasons. However, I get extremely self-conscious and constantly worry that people are staring at and judging my jawline and the crooked side of my face.
Have you ever had any other unusual beliefs or experiences, like hearing voices, feeling watched or followed, or believing people are trying to harm you for reasons unrelated to your appearance?

No, I have never experienced anything like hearing voices, feeling followed, or believing that anyone wants to harm me. My only concern is really just about how crooked my face looks and trying to hide my jawline from the wrong angles.
Have you ever had any other fixed beliefs that are clearly untrue, like feeling that people are trying to spy on, harm, or control you, or hearing voices that others do not hear?
No, I have never experienced anything like that. I have never heard any voices that others couldn't hear, and I've never felt like people were trying to spy on, harm, or control me.

Have you ever had any other unusual beliefs or experiences, such as hearing voices that others cannot hear, feeling that people are spying on you, or believing you have been specially targeted for harm?
No, I have never heard voices, felt spied on, or felt targeted in any way. My only concern is really just how crooked my face and jawline look to other people.

final_diagnosis.reason: The presentation is most consistent with hypochondriacal/overvalued somatic preoccupation in the ICD-10 candidate set, but the interview most strongly supports body dysmorphic disorder-type psychopathology: persistent preoccupation with a perceived facial defect (crooked face/weird jawline), repetitive checking/zooming in on photos, marked distress, and avoidance of social situations due to appearance concerns. Insight is poor to absent, but there are no other psychotic symptoms, no contamination/order obsessions, and the concern is narrowly focused on appearance.
